title: Raghuraj Singh Rana vs Anita Singh on 4 May, 2024
full_text: Raghuraj Singh Rana vs Anita Singh on 4 May, 2024 CA No. 151/2021 Raghuraj Rana Vs. Anita Singh IN THE COURT OF MANU GOEL KHARB: SPECIAL JUDGE (NDPS-02) SOUTH WEST DISTRICT DWARKA COURTS:NEW DELHI Criminal Appeal No. 151/2021 CNR No. DLSW01-011436-2021 In the Matter of : Raghuraj Singh Rana S/o Sh. Kartar Singh Rana R/o RZF-27, Mahavir Enclave New Delhi ....Petitioner Versus Anita Singh W/o Sh. Dev Kumar, R/o RZF-57, Street No. 4, Mahavir Enclave, New Delhi ....Respondent Date of Institution of the Appeal : 22.11.2021 Date of Arguments : 01.05.2024 Date of Judgment : 04.05.2024 JUDGMENT: 1. Vide this judgment, I shall dispose of the present appeal under Section 374 Cr.P.C. filed by the appellant against the order of conviction and order on sentence dated 06.04.2021 and 22.10.2021 passed by Sh. Abhinav Ahlawat, Ld. MM Dwarka Courts, New Delhi in case bearing CC No. 4989246/2016 titled as "Anita Singh Vs Raghuraj Singh Rana" whereby accused was convicted and CNR No. DLSW01-011436-2021 Page 1 of 17 CA No. 151/2021 Raghuraj Rana Vs. Anita Singh sentenced to undergo two months simple imprisonment and to pay compensation of Rs. 3 lakhs as fine to the complainant within period of 30 days and in default of the accused in making payment of compensation amount within period of 30 days, the accused shall undergo further simple imprisonment of 1 month. 2. Appellant herein was the accused before the Ld. Trial Court and the respondent was the complainant before the Ld. Trial Court. For the sake of convenience, both the parties shall be addressed by the same nomenclature by which they were addressed before the Ld. Trial Court. 3. Brief facts of the case are that the accused and his wife had approached the complainant for a friendly loan of Rs. 4,50,000/- (Rupees Four Lacs and Fifty Thousand only) as this was required by the accused for construction of property in collaboration with a builder. It is further stated that being in friendly relations with the accused, complainant gave the said amount to the accused and accused had voluntarily agreed to return the said amount within a year alongwith interest @ 2% per month. It is stated that as per the terms agreed between the parties, in the month of February 2015, when the complainant approached CNR No. DLSW01-011436-2021 Page 2 of 17 CA No. 151/2021 Raghuraj Rana Vs. Anita Singh the accused to return the loan amount, wife of the accused had issued a cheque bearing no. 0392465 for Rs. 1,50,000/- dated 16.02.2015 drawn on Oriental Bank of Commerce, Mahvir Enclave, New Delhi and the accused further promised to pay the balance amount after a month. Thereafter, in April 2015 complainant had further contacted the accused and his wife for remaining amount and accused issued a post dated cheque bearing no. 172886 for Rs. 2,00,000/- (Rupees Two Lacs only) dated 25.05.2015 drawn on SBI, Palam, Dabri Mor and requested for some time for the remaining amount. It is further stated that the accused had assured the complainant that the cheque shall be honored at the time of its presentation but when the complainant presented the cheque in question for encashment, same got dishonoured with the remarks "Refer to drawer" vide cheque return memo dated 18.08.2015 Ex. CW1/2. Thereafter, complainant initially contacted and requested the accused for making payment of cheque amount. However, the accused did not pay any heed to the demand made by the complainant and started avoiding the complainant on one pretext or the other. Thereafter, complainant sent a legal demand notice dated 08.09.2015 Ex. PW1/3 to the appellant/accused within the stipulated period of 30 days through CNR No. DLSW01-011436-2021 Page 3 of 17 CA No. 151/2021 Raghuraj Rana Vs. Anita Singh speed post but accused failed to make the payment within the stipulated period. Thereafter, the complainant filed the complaint case under Section 138 of NI Act and led the pre-summoning evidence. 4. The accused was summoned and notice under Section 251 Cr.P.C. was framed against him to which he pleaded not guilty and claimed trial and took the defence that he borrowed a loan of Rs. 5 lacs from the complainant in the year 2014 and he had already repaid Rs. 2.5 lacs out of the said loan towards principal and Rs. 1,70,000/- towards interest. He stated that the complainant at the time of advancing the loan had obtained the cheque of Rs. 5 lacs from him as a security and after part repayment, the complainant returned the said cheque and obtained two more cheques from him for Rs. 2 lacs and Rs. 1 lac. He further stated that he could not repay the remaining loan amount due to loss in business. He further stated that he did not receive any legal notice sent by the complainant. 5. The complainant led post summoning evidence in which he adopted his pre-summoning evidence affidavit Ex. CW1/A and relied upon the documents Ex. CW1/1 to Ex. CW1/5. Ld. Counsel CNR No. DLSW01-011436-2021 Page 4 of 17 CA No. 151/2021 Raghuraj Rana Vs. Anita Singh for accused duly cross examined the complainant. Thereafter, complainant examined CW-2 Sh. Dev Kumar and he was also duly cross examined by the ld. Defence counsel and thereafter the complainant evidence was closed. 6. Thereafter, statement of accused u/s 281 read with Section 313 Cr.P.C. was recorded in which all the incriminating evidence was put to the accused to which he stated that he never approached the complainant for any loan of any amount. He further stated that he do not even know how the impugned cheque came into the hands of the complainant. He stated that his daughter used to visit the shop of complainant and the said impugned cheque has been misused by the complainant after taking it from his office as the complainant used to visit his office regularly. He further averred that he did not owe any liability towards the complainant and the complainant has misused the abovesaid cheque. 7. Accused chose not to lead defence evidence and thereafter the matter was listed for final arguments. 8. Arguments were advanced by ld. Counsels for both the parties. CNR No. DLSW01-011436-2021 Page 5 of 17 CA No. 151/2021 Raghuraj Rana Vs. Anita Singh 9. After hearing arguments, Ld. Trial Court vide its impugned judgment dated 06.04.2021 convicted the accused and sentenced him to undergo simple imprisonment for two months and to pay a fine of Rs. 3 lakhs to be payable to the complainant as compensation within period of 30 days and in default of payment of compensation amount, the accused shall undergo simple imprisonment of 1 month. 10. Feeling aggrieved, the accused has challenged the impugned order of conviction and sentence by filing the present appeal on the grounds mentioned below : (i) Ld. Trial court failed to appreciate the fact that the cheque in question was not issued in discharge of liability by the appellant and the complainant misused the cheque in question and further abused the process of law. (ii) That the Ld. Trial Court did not appreciate properly and correctly the evidence on record as well as judgment given in favour of wife of accused where Neelam Rana was acquitted. Hence the same is improper and unjustified. (iii) That the Ld. Trial Court sentenced the accused illegally and directed him to pay Rs. 3,00,000/- as fine to complainant which is very high and Trial Court may award cheque amount plus 10% while deciding the case. Hence, the impugned judgment and order on sentence is liable to be set aside or altered in favour of appellant. CNR No. DLSW01-011436-2021 Page 6 of 17 CA No. 151/2021 Raghuraj Rana Vs. Anita Singh 11. Case file and trial court record perused. Detailed arguments heard on behalf of both the parties. 12. It is trite in law that in a prosecution under Section 138 NI Act, the statutory presumption under Section 118 & 139 NI Act stands in favour of the complainant and once the complainant proves that negotiable instrument/cheque is executed by the maker in favour of the holder of the cheque, the law presumes that the same is drawn for consideration and the holder of the cheque received it in discharge of any debt or legal liability. Thereafter, the burden shifts on the accused to prove the contrary, which he can do so by demolishing the credit of the complainant through his cross examination or by leading any cogent evidence in his defence and the burden on the accused is only of preponderance of probabilities and not as heavy as that on the prosecution. 13. The Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in " K. Bhaskaran Vs. Sankaran Vaidhya Balan (1999) 7 SCC 510 summarized the ingredients of the offence U/s 138 NI Act . The relevant extract is reproduced below for ready reference :- "The offence U/s 138 of the Act can be completed only with the CNR No. DLSW01-011436-2021 Page 7 of 17 CA No. 151/2021 Raghuraj Rana Vs. Anita Singh concatenation of a number of acts. The following are the acts which are components of the said offence: (1) drawing of the cheque, (2) presentation of the cheque to the banker, (3) returning of the cheque unpaid by the drawee bank, (4) giving notice in writing to the drawer of the cheque demanding the payment of the cheque amount, (5) failure of the drawer to make the payment within 15 days of the receipt of notice." 14. As per record, the cheque in question was signed by the accused and the same was presented by the complainant to his banker but the cheque was returned unpaid by the bank with remarks 'Refer to Drawer' and despite service of legal notice, the accused did not pay the cheque amount to the complainant within stipulated period of 15 days. Hence, the dishonor of the cheque in question and the filing of the complaint within stipulated period in this case is not under dispute. 15. The accused has not admitted the receiving of the legal demand notice served by the complainant. Under the provision of Section 138 of NI Act, not only the giving of notice but also the receipt of notice has to be proved by the complainant. The Hon'ble Supreme Court of India has judicially recognized the 'deemed or constructive service of notice' in various decisions. In the case of K. CNR No. DLSW01-011436-2021 Page 8 of 17 CA No. 151/2021 Raghuraj Rana Vs. Anita Singh Bhaskar Vs. Sankaran Vaidhyan Balan AIR 1999 SC 3762, it was held that : "If a strict interpretation is given that the drawer should have actually received the notice for the period of 15 days to start running no matter that the payee sent the notice on the correct address, a trickster cheque drawer would get the premium to avoid receiving the notice by different strategies and he could escape from the legal consequences of Section 138 of the Act. It must be borne in mind that the court should not adopt an interpretation which helps a dishonest evader and clips an honest payee as that would defeat the very legislative measure" 16. Furthermore, it was held by Hon'ble Supreme Court of India that in cases where the notice is returned as unclaimed, such date would be the commencing date in reckoning the period of 15 days as envisaged under proviso (c) of Section 138 NI Act. 17. In the present case, complainant had issued the legal demand notice to the accused within the statutory period. Further, it has been rightly observed by the Ld. Trial Court that service was effected upon the accused at the address which was mentioned by the accused in the bail bond furnished by him before the Ld. Trial Court and as such the legal notice is deemed to have been served upon the accused. CNR No. DLSW01-011436-2021 Page 9 of 17 CA No. 151/2021 Raghuraj Rana Vs. Anita Singh 18. Hence, complainant has been able to establish that the accused had failed to make the payment against the dishonored cheques within the stipulated period despite the service of legal demand notice and therefore, all the ingredients of the offence under Section 138 NI Act are proved. 19. Complainant has discharged her burden of a prima facie case by leading evidence and by satisfying the basic ingredients of Section 138 NI Act and now the burden shifted upon the accused to rebut the presumption under Section 118 and 139 of NI Act operating in favour of the complainant. 20. Once the complainant was able to satisfy all the ingredients of the offence, the onus shifted upon the accused to prove his defence. Ld. counsel for the accused has taken two lines of defence. The first line of defence is that the accused had taken a loan of Rs. 5 lacs from the complainant in the year 2014 and had given a cheque of Rs. 5 lac as security cheque and after part repayment, complainant returned the security cheque of Rs. 5 lacs and obtained two more cheques of Rs. 2 lacs and 1 lac each from the accused. The accused claimed that he had made part repayment of the loan to the complainant and the present cheque was issued by way of security CNR No. DLSW01-011436-2021 Page 10 of 17 CA No. 151/2021 Raghuraj Rana Vs. Anita Singh and not in discharge of any legal liability towards the complainant but the accused has not filed any documents to show that he had repaid the loan amount to the complainant whereas the complainant has filed copy of her bank passbook Ex. CW1/6 to show that she had transferred Rs. 2 lacs into the account of Ms. Heena Rana who is the daughter of present accused. Complainant also deposed that remaining loan amount was transferred to the accused from the bank account of husband of the complainant. Also, complainant has been able to show that she had given loan to the accused by making payment in the account of daughter of the accused but on the contrary, accused is unable to file any document to show that he had made part repayment of the loan amount. Moreover, during cross-examination of the complainant also, no suggestion was given to the complainant that the accused had already made payment towards the cheque in question. 21. Assuming that the cheque in question was a security cheque, the accused would still have a liability to pay. A security cheque is simply a post dated cheque issued to a payee as a security for availing the option to present the same in case where the drawer fails to fulfill the future obligations arising from a transaction or a CNR No. DLSW01-011436-2021 Page 11 of 17 CA No. 151/2021 Raghuraj Rana Vs. Anita Singh business deal. A security cheque acts as a surety for the person accepting such cheque and it is now a settled law that dishonor of a post dated cheque i.e. a security cheque attracts culpability u/s 138 NI Act. The only test for application of Section 138 is whether there was a legally enforceable debt on the date mentioned in the cheque. In the case of 'Sripati Singh Vs. State of Jharkhand', Crl. A. No. 1269, 1270 of 2021, the division bench of the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India opined that where a cheque is issued as security for a time specific loan, on default of repayment of loan the security cheque issued would mature, if then the security cheque is dishonored the consequences contemplated Section 138 of NI Act and other provisions of NI Act would flow. 22. The second line of defence taken by the accused as mentioned in his statement u/s 313 Cr.P.C. is that the accused never took any loan from the complainant and that the son of the accused used to work with the complainant and that the complainant took the cheque in question from the office of accused as complainant used to regularly visit the office of the accused. So far as the second line of defence taken by the accused is concerned, the accused has admitted his signatures on the cheque in question, CNR No. DLSW01-011436-2021 Page 12 of 17 CA No. 151/2021 Raghuraj Rana Vs. Anita Singh hence, the issuance of cheque in question is not in dispute but the accused raised a plea that the cheque was taken by the complainant from the office of the accused as the complainant used to visit his office regularly. 23. It is also a matter of record that the accused has not lodged any criminal complaint or FIR against the complainant regarding stealing of the cheque in question and misusing it. Any reasonable prudent person faced with similar circumstances would be prompt in lodging an FIR, but the accused chose not to do so. There is no 100 number call made to the police and simply a suggestion was given to the complainant during her cross-examination that she had misused the cheque by taking it from someone else. In view of the above facts and circumstances, it has been rightly observed by the Ld. Trial Court that the accused has failed to discharge his burden. Even after the complainant lodged the prosecution against the accused under Section 138 NI Act, the accused still did not file any complaint before the police or in the court against the alleged theft of cheque by the complainant whereas the accused could have taken the assistance of police on the same day when the complainant had allegedly CNR No. DLSW01-011436-2021 Page 13 of 17 CA No. 151/2021 Raghuraj Rana Vs. Anita Singh stolen the cheque in question from the office of the accused. 24. Otherwise also, it is evident that both the defences taken by the accused are contradictory to each other. On one hand the accused admits that he had taken loan from the complainant whereas on the other hand he declined having taken any loan from the complainant. Similarly, at one place, the accused states that he had issued two cheques of 2 lacs and 1 lac in favor of the complainant whereas at the other place he states that he had never issued any cheque to the complainant. 25. So, the accused has failed to show that he had no liability towards the complainant or that he had issued the cheque as a security cheque rather he has himself admitted that he had to repay some amount to the complainant. Hence, the defence raised by the accused that the cheque in question was misused by the complainant miserably fails. 26. Hence, the appeal is liable to be dismissed solely on the ground of failure of the accused to show that he has already made the payment to the complainant towards the cheque in question. CNR No. DLSW01-011436-2021 Page 14 of 17 CA No. 151/2021 Raghuraj Rana Vs. Anita Singh 27. In the present case, the accused has miserably failed to prove any of his defence rather he himself admitted at the stage of notice that he had issued two cheques of Rs. 2 lacs and Rs. 1 lac respectively in favour of the complainant towards part repayment of the loan taken from him. 28. In the present case, the accused has not been able to establish his defence either through his own evidence or by way of impeaching the credit of complainant's witnesses and it appears that he raised a false defence in order to avoid his legal liability towards the complainant for the cheque in question. Consequently, there is hardly any ground to interfere with the judgment of conviction given by the Ld. Trial Court. Thereafter, grounds of appeal taken by the accused is rejected. 29. Ld. Trial Court has passed a well-reasoned and detailed judgment discussing all the contentions raised by both the parties. In view of the above, the court does not find any reason to interfere in the impugned judgment dated 06.04.2021 passed by the Ld. Trial Court. The judgment of Ld. Trial Court is well reasoned and passed a legally sound decision and observes to be upheld. CNR No. DLSW01-011436-2021 Page 15 of 17 CA No. 151/2021 Raghuraj Rana Vs. Anita Singh 30. So far as the sentence is concerned, Ld. Trial Court has sentenced the appellant to two months simple imprisonment and to pay Rs. 3 lacs as fine which shall be paid to the complainant as compensation. The convict is further directed to pay the fine within 30 days and in default, he shall undergo further simple imprisonment in default for one month. 31. Complainant/respondent Anita Singh submits that she has also settled her all other pending matters with the appellant for full and final of sum of Rs. 7 lacs and that she has no objection, if the court shows leniency and reduces the sentence awarded to the accused to only pay fine/compensation amount of cheque in question i.e. Rs. 2 lacs. 32. After hearing the submissions of the parties, the court is of the view that as the appellant is trmorseful for his act and has already paid Rs. 5 lacs out of the total amount of Rs. 7 lacs, hence, a lenient view can be taken. Accordingly, order on sentence dated 22.10.2021 is modified and imprisonment of two months awarded by the Ld. Trial Court is set aside. Appellant/accused is directed to pay a fine of Rs. 2,00,000/- to the complainant/respondent within a week from today CNR No. DLSW01-011436-2021 Page 16 of 17 CA No. 151/2021 Raghuraj Rana Vs. Anita Singh and in default to undergo imprisonment for 30 days. 33. The appeal filed by the accused Raghuraj Singh Rana is hereby dismissed with the aforesaid modification on the quantum of sentence. 34. Trial court record be sent back to the Ld. Trial Court/Successor court alongwith a copy of this judgment. 35. Appeal file be consigned to record room after due compliance. Pronounced in the open Court today Digitally signed by i.e. 04.05.2024 Manu Goel Manu Goel Kharb Kharb Date: 2024.05.04 16:44:33 +0530 (Manu Goel Kharb) Spl.
